text: When setting project goals, using the SMART framework is essential. This means your objectives should be Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound. For example, instead of saying "improve the website," a SMART goal is "increase page load speed by 20% within three months." Once your main goal is clear, break it down into smaller milestones. These are checkpoints that help you track progress and stay motivated. Each milestone should have clear deliverables, which are the tangible results or outputs you produce, such as a report or a new feature. Finally, ensure stakeholder alignment. This means regularly communicating with everyone involved—from your team to your clients—to confirm that the goals and deliverables meet their expectations and needs.
